name: filesystem-mcp
description: Filesystem MCP server for AI assistants.
long_description: Reads, writes, searches, diffs, and patches files inside the directories you choose. Paths outside those directories are refused unless you approve access when asked, and sensitive files such as `.env`, `*.pem`, and SSH keys are denied by default. Content search uses RE2, so no pattern can hang the server. Requires Node.js 24 or later.

tools.name: list_roots
tools.description: List the allowed directories. Call this first.

tools.name: list
tools.description: List directory contents as entries and an ASCII tree.

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Find files by glob pattern, such as **/*.ts.

tools.name: stat
tools.description: Get size, modified time, permissions, MIME type, and a token estimate.

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Search file contents with RE2 regex or literal text.

tools.name: diff
tools.description: Compare two files as a unified diff.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read text files whole, by line range, head, or tail.

tools.name: create
tools.description: Create, overwrite, or append to text files, or make empty directories.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Apply literal string replacements to files.

tools.name: move
tools.description: Move, rename, or copy files and directories.

tools.name: replace_text
tools.description: Search and replace across files matching a glob.

tools.name: patch
tools.description: Apply a unified diff to one file.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Revert earlier file changes by undo id or the last N calls.

allowed_directories.title: Allowed folders
allowed_directories.description: The folders the AI can use. The AI must ask you before it opens anything else.

read_only.title: Read-only mode
read_only.description: Turn this on so the AI can read files but never change, move, or delete them.

read_only_folders.title: Read-only folders
read_only_folders.description: Optional. Folders the AI can read but not change. Each one must be in Allowed folders or inside one of them. Has no effect while Read-only mode is on, because then nothing can be changed.

read_only_dirs.title: Read-only folders, typed (older setting)
read_only_dirs.description: Optional. Folders saved here keep working, together with Read-only folders above. Use the setting above for new folders. To type more than one, put a semicolon between the full paths on Windows or a colon on macOS and Linux, with no space after it. Examples: C:\Work\docs;C:\Work\archive or /Users/me/docs:/Users/me/archive

deny_patterns.title: Extra blocked files
deny_patterns.description: Optional. Files the AI can never open, with a comma between each. To block a folder, add /** after its name. The example private/**, *.sqlite, salaries.xlsx blocks everything in any folder named private, every .sqlite file, and every file named salaries.xlsx in any folder. Files such as .env, private keys, and cloud and SSH credentials are already blocked. Full list: https://github.com/j0hanz/filesystem-mcp/blob/main/docs/configuration.md#secret-files

allow_patterns.title: Unblocked secret files
allow_patterns.description: Optional. Leave this empty unless the AI needs a file that is blocked by default. List the files with a comma between each. The example .env.example, debug.keystore unblocks those two names. The AI can then read and change any file with a listed name, in every allowed folder, so list only what you are happy for it to touch. Anything in Extra blocked files stays blocked. Full list: https://github.com/j0hanz/filesystem-mcp/blob/main/docs/configuration.md#secret-files
